record.title: RegimeAbstain estimates multi-hop retrieval failure from query and ANN structure
record.summary: The September 2026 RegimeAbstain preprint models retrieval confidence from query and approximate-nearest-neighbor structure, without an extra language-model call, then abstains on risky multi-hop retrievals. Across three benchmarks and two retrieval architectures, the authors report confident-wrong-answer rates of 14.5%–62.1%. On MuSiQue with an LLM-judge pipeline, they report reducing that rate from 39.5% to 20.6% at 50% coverage, with expected calibration error 0.035.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA and HoVer under LLM-judge and dense-only retrieval, authors report best or tied-best AUC-AC in five tested conditions against eight confidence baselines. On MuSiQue with an LLM-judge pipeline, CWAR falls from 39.5% to 20.6% at 50% coverage (47.8% relative reduction); ECE is 0.035. Training on MuSiQue transfers to 2WikiMultiHopQA with a reported 0.5 percentage-point AUC loss.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv record identifies the paper and its submission/revision metadata. This confirms that the preprint was posted, not that its experimental claims have been independently established.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the risk-coverage, calibration or baseline comparisons was inspected.
No system-level utility accounting or retrieval-stack shift test was inspected.

brief.importance_rationale: If reproduced across retrieval stacks, low-cost retrieval-stage confidence could help systems abstain before generating from incomplete evidence. The strongest reported result is benchmark-specific and serves only half the queries, so its consequence is meaningful but bounded.
limitations: The metrics and results are reported by the preprint authors; no independent reproduction was inspected.
The 20.6% CWAR result is at 50% coverage, so half of queries are abstained or escalated; the paper does not establish the resulting operational utility or total cost.
The paper reports substantially weaker feature-success information in dense-only retrieval, and the dominant ANN feature differs between benchmark regimes.
Training-distribution transfer across two named datasets does not establish robustness to production corpus, retriever, embedding-model or query-mix changes.

technical.claimed_result: Across MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA and HoVer under LLM-judge and dense-only retrieval, authors report best or tied-best AUC-AC in five tested conditions against eight confidence baselines. On MuSiQue with an LLM-judge pipeline, CWAR falls from 39.5% to 20.6% at 50% coverage (47.8% relative reduction); ECE is 0.035. technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv preprint and its method/experimental design were inspected. The numerical outcome is reported by the paper authors and is not independently demonstrated in this review.
technical.mechanism: A logistic Retrieval Confidence Score combines up to nine query and ANN structural features to estimate retrieval success and support a calibrated abstention policy without another LLM call. The paper formalizes conditions under which retrieval features carry information about confident failure and reports different predictive features across datasets.
technical.regime: Author-run experiments on three multi-hop QA datasets, two retrieval architectures and five failure regimes; strongest CWAR result uses MuSiQue with an LLM-judge pipeline at 50% query coverage.
technical.strongest_baseline: Eight confidence baselines across five conditions; the highlighted MuSiQue comparison reports CWAR 39.5% baseline versus 20.6% RCS at 50% coverage. No independent system-level or utility reproduction inspected.

brief.title: RegimeAbstain estimates multi-hop retrieval failure from query and ANN structure
brief.why_it_matters: Retrieval failures can originate upstream of answer generation. A signal computed from the retriever’s own score structure could expose some incomplete evidence sets before a model confidently answers, but abstention trades errors for reduced service coverage and the paper finds weaker signals in dense-only settings.
